articles.title: Columbia’s Michael Zheng comes full circle as Americans advance at US Open
articles.summary: Former Ivy League star wins US Open debut. Shelton and Tiafoe advance to third round. Pegula cruises past Kenin in 56 minutes. Michael Zheng spent years making the long trek from northern New Jersey, first by bus across the Hudson River to the Port Authority bus terminal and then nearly the full…
body: The 22-year-old American wildcard and two-time NCAA champion from nearby Columbia University brushed aside Hungary’s Fabian Marozsan 6-4, 6-4, 6-2 to win his rain-interrupted US Open debut, providing one of the more unlikely highlights on a busy day for the home contingent in New York.

Playing before a vocal crowd of his college teammates and alumni who splashed the intimate confines of Court 10 with blue and white, Zheng needed only 1hr 51min to dispatch of the world No 63, breaking five times and dropping serve only once. He hit nearly twice as many winners (33) as unforced errors (17) and was especially ruthless on his first serve, winning all but three of 39 points (92.3%) over three sets.
“It just felt like a college tennis match, really,” Zheng said. “My teammates came out. They had the ‘Let’s go, Michael’ chants, and I’m not sure my opponent was ready for it.”

He added: “This is a place I grew up training. It was one of the first places that I kind of called home base, actually, the Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. So it’s really special to get that first main-draw win here and in front of my family, friends and teammates as well.”

articles.title: Premier League paradox: midfielders are more and more expensive, yet more and more mediocre | Jonathan Liew
articles.summary: Enzo Fernández and Sandro Tonali had big-money summer moves, but can they hold a candle to past greats? Perhaps the only thing you really need to know about the modern midfield role is that Enzo Maresca reckons that Marc Guéhi can play it better than Mateo Kovacic.
body: This is the only real way of explaining the vastly inflated fee City have paid Chelsea in a race where they were the only realistic bidder. Angelo Stiller at Stuttgart – to pluck one name out of the ether – is a similar profile of midfielder of the same age who would probably have been available at half the price, and with exactly one fewer video in which he was filmed making racist and homophobic slurs. But unlike Stiller, Fernández is battle-hardened, Premier League-proven, a known known. Whatever flaws he possesses – from his slow recovery speed to occasional fits of petulance to his intolerance – have been priced in.

articles.title: Will 'proper captain's performance' be springboard for Shankland?
articles.summary: Lawrence Shankland nets twice in Rangers' 2-1 success at Falkirk, making it back-to-back wins after a sticky start to the campaign for the new-look Ibrox side.
body: On a night where plenty of his team-mates were panicking, Lawrence Shankland was a figure of calm for Rangers in Falkirk.
His two goals were decisive for Derek McInnes' side, earning a second Scottish Premiership win of the season days after the captain's penalty delivered the first at Pittodrie.
In an error-strewn game that lacked quality, Shankland was the difference maker.
His first whistled into the roof of the net off his weaker left foot, while his second - again on his left - was passed into the bottom corner with the game on a knife edge.

articles.summary: Olympic champion targets third Games in LA. Michael Jordan narrates announcement video. Chiles joins Lee and Carey on comeback trail. Jordan Chiles is returning for a run at her third Olympics, ⁠announcing Wednesday she intends to compete in the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
body: Chiles shared ⁠her decision ⁠in ​a video narrated by basketball legend Michael Jordan.
Chiles, 25, owns a 2024 gold medal ‌from Paris and a 2021 silver from Tokyo in team competitions.

She won an individual bronze in 2024 on floor exercise before the medal was taken away by the Court of Arbitration for Sport and ‌given to Romania’s Ana Barbosu after a score inquiry. Chiles appealed the decision to the ​CAS and awaits a ruling.
Chiles starred at UCLA and won two NCAA titles in floor exercise (2023, 2026) and two others on bars (2023, 2025). She is a 23-time ⁠All-American who recorded 19 perfect-10s.

articles.title: 'Humble but ambitious' - the return of fallen giants Schalke
articles.summary: One of Germany's fallen giants, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga after a complicated few years.
body: On matchday, even for friendlies, Gelsenkirchen pauses as locals turn their attention to Schalke's Veltins-Arena.
Everywhere you look, swathes of fans in blue and white are arriving by tram, on foot or by car.
In the team's first game back in the Bundesliga for three years, 6,000 away fans stayed after the final whistle to support the players despite a 3-0 defeat at Augsburg.
"It's a kind of religious feeling that people have towards Schalke," said Professor Frank Eckardt, who grew up in the Schalke-Nord area.

articles.title: Girona and Xocolates Torras renew their sponsorship agreement until 2028
articles.summary: Girona FC and Xocolates Torras have renewed their sponsorship agreement for two more seasons, until the end of the 2027/28 season. In this way, the two entities continue a relationship that began in 2023 and strengthen an alliance based on their connection to the region and shared values.
body: With this renewal, Xocolates Torras will continue to be an Official Sponsor of Girona FC and will maintain its association with the Club's various teams. The brand will continue to have a prominent presence on the women's team kits, with its logo placed on the upper back of the jersey, above the number.

The renewal consolidates a relationship that unites two entities deeply connected to the Girona region. Based in Cornellà del Terri and with over 135 years of history, Xocolates Torras is a leading company in the chocolate sector, with a strong international focus while maintaining its roots in the region.

During the initial years of collaboration, the relationship between the two entities has strengthened this connection and brought both brands closer to their audiences, with initiatives such as the official Girona FC chocolate range.

articles.title: Fabio Wardley defends Moses Itauma coach after major setback against Filip Hrgovic
articles.summary: Fabio Wardley has leapt to the defence of coach Ben Davison after teammate Moses Itauma failed in his bid to become the second-youngest ever world heavyweight champion on Saturday.
body: Itauma punched himself out after a dominant eight rounds against Filip Hrgovic at London’s O2 Arena, appearing visibly exhausted against the Croatian in the ninth before his corner threw in the towel.

The 21-year-old had admitted pre-fight that he had never gone 12 rounds in sparring, which after the result ignited a torrent of backlash towards his gym as questions were raised about his preparations.

Wardley, who is also trained by Davison, lost his first fight to Daniel Dubois in similar fashion, gassing late on after dominating the early stages, and will now rematch “Dynamite” looking to regain his WBO title on 17 October.
But when speaking about the criticism his trainer has received, Wardley dismissed the noise as “delusional” and said he is ready to prove the gym’s worth by delivering greatness.

articles.title: Shields or Taylor the greatest? "We're 1A and 1B!"
articles.summary: Claressa Shields has hailed the greatness of Katie Taylor and says she holds no qualms over a fight between the boxing greats never materialising.
body: Claressa Shields and Amanda Serrano both wished Katie Taylor a happy retirement as the Irish great prepares for the final bout of her professional career this weekend; Shields played down the idea she was upset the two never shared the ring, praising Taylor's historic career.
Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans.
The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history.
Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport.

articles.title: What happens to Kawhi Leonard’s Toronto Raptors trade revealed after NBA announces punishment
articles.summary: Amid all the noise surrounding Kawhi Leonard and the Los Angeles Clippers after the NBA’s ruling, Shams Charania has revealed the status of his move to the Toronto Raptors. The Los Angeles Clippers and Kawhi Leonard have been under NBA investigation for salary cap circumvention for nearly a year.
body: The franchise is facing severe punishments including forfeiture of first-round picks and bans for top executives. Leonard himself has gotten off relatively easy with a $700K fine.
Even before all this came out, Kawhi and the Clips had already agreed to move on, and a trade was agreed with the Toronto Raptors. Following the NBA’s verdict, there is an update on that situation.
The NBA had announced that any punishment Kawhi faced as a result of the investigation would carry over if he joined a new team. As such, his trade to the Raptors had been put on hold.
However, the player himself is facing no suspensions or time missed in this scenario. And as such, Shams Charania has explained what the future of his move looks like.

articles.title: Spanish wonderkid Jodar in testy exchange after shock US Open exit
articles.summary: Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar was involved in a testy exchange with a journalist following his stunning exit to Chinese lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete at the US Open on Wednesday.
body: Jodar was tripped up at the first hurdle of his maiden ‌campaign in New York, as the Spanish 12th seed failed to find his rhythm and fell 6-2 6-1 ‌6-1 to Bu.

Back at the site of his junior triumph two ​years ago, 19-year-old Jodar looked unusually out of sorts after his first-round clash was delayed by a day due to ​rain, with a flurry of unforced errors in defeat.

Jodar, one of the fastest-rising talents in the ‌men's game after going from 362nd in the world to 13th over the past year, continued to struggle for answers and even sent several of his rackets to be re-strung in a bid to change his fortunes.

But it proved futile, with ⁠the 24-year-old Bu refusing to loosen his grip on the contest ​as he took the first set before sealing the second set after another unforced ​error from Jodar to silence a vocal contingent of Spanish supporters ​on Court 17.
